package_metadata.file_role: core concepts and canonical review gate

core_concepts.name: Canonical HCD review gate
core_concepts.summary: A single reusable gate for broad human-centered design review; individual records reference this rather than repeating it.
questions: What goal are they trying to accomplish?
What signifiers indicate where or how to act?
What does the user believe will happen?
How well does action map to effect?
What knowledge exists in the world?
What invalid or dangerous actions are allowed?
Is the observed failure a slip or a mistake?
Can the user recover without expert help?
What observed user evidence supports the diagnosis?
use_when: A broad workflow, screenshot, form, or dashboard needs initial diagnosis.
do_not_overextend_when: A record has a narrower mechanism such as delayed feedback or mode error; use the specific record first.

source_traceability.source_file: The Design of Everyday Things Revised and Expanded Edition.epub(1).zip
source_traceability.book_title: The Design of Everyday Things: Revised and Expanded Edition
source_traceability.author: Don Norman
directly_supported_claims: Discoverability concerns whether people can determine possible actions and current state.
Feedback gives information about what action has been done and what result occurred.
Mappings relate controls or actions to the effects they produce.
Constraints reduce the set of possible actions.
Conceptual models help people predict what actions are possible and how the system will respond.
inferred_claims: This review gate combines multiple source concepts for AI-agent diagnostic use.

derivation.explanation: The broad checklist is centralized to prevent universal-template repetition in individual records.

core_concepts.name: Discoverability of possible action and state
core_concepts.summary: People need enough perceivable information to know what can be done and what state exists.
core_concepts.distinct_diagnostic_value: Use when the user cannot identify available action or current state before acting.
observable_user_behavior: Hesitates at a step with no obvious next action
Opens instructions for a repeated task
Clicks exploratory controls to see what is possible
core_concepts.specific_design_decision: Whether action/state cues need to be made perceivable at the point of need.

source_traceability.source_file: The Design of Everyday Things Revised and Expanded Edition.epub(1).zip
source_traceability.book_title: The Design of Everyday Things: Revised and Expanded Edition
source_traceability.author: Don Norman
directly_supported_claims: Discoverability concerns whether people can determine possible actions and current state.

derivation.explanation: This record keeps discoverability distinct from later understanding or feedback.

core_concepts.name: Understanding of operation and result
core_concepts.summary: A user may find an action but still misunderstand what it does or what the result means.
core_concepts.distinct_diagnostic_value: Use when action is visible but prediction or interpretation is wrong.
observable_user_behavior: Chooses a visible action for the wrong reason
Cannot explain result after completion
Asks what a visible state means
core_concepts.specific_design_decision: Whether the system image needs clearer explanation, naming, or feedback content.

source_traceability.source_file: The Design of Everyday Things Revised and Expanded Edition.epub(1).zip
source_traceability.book_title: The Design of Everyday Things: Revised and Expanded Edition
source_traceability.author: Don Norman
directly_supported_claims: Understanding concerns whether people can interpret meaning, operation, and results.
Conceptual models help people predict what actions are possible and how the system will respond.

derivation.explanation: This separates finding an action from understanding its meaning.

core_concepts.name: Seven stages of action as diagnostic sequence
core_concepts.summary: A task can fail at goal formation, intention, action specification, execution, perception, interpretation, or evaluation.
core_concepts.distinct_diagnostic_value: Use to locate where a workflow breaks rather than labeling the whole experience as confusing.
observable_user_behavior: States a correct goal but chooses no action
Acts correctly but cannot interpret result
Repeats action because state is unclear
core_concepts.specific_design_decision: Which stage needs design support: action choice, execution, feedback, interpretation, or evaluation.

source_traceability.source_file: The Design of Everyday Things Revised and Expanded Edition.epub(1).zip
source_traceability.book_title: The Design of Everyday Things: Revised and Expanded Edition
source_traceability.author: Don Norman
directly_supported_claims: The gulf of execution concerns forming and carrying out an action to meet a goal.
The gulf of evaluation concerns perceiving and interpreting system state after action.

derivation.explanation: The action-cycle taxonomy anchors the execution/evaluation split.

core_concepts.name: Human-centered design starts with observed people and real tasks
core_concepts.summary: Design reasoning must begin from people’s goals, context, abilities, and observed behavior, not from the implementation alone.
core_concepts.distinct_diagnostic_value: Use when a design recommendation lacks user/task evidence.
observable_user_behavior: Repeated failures cluster around one step
Operators create workarounds
Training compensates for routine system gaps
core_concepts.specific_design_decision: Whether to observe, prototype, test, or reframe before prescribing a fix.

source_traceability.author: Don Norman
directly_supported_claims: Human-centered design begins with understanding people, their needs, abilities, and context.
Design improves through cycles of observation, prototyping, testing, and revision.

derivation.explanation: This records the source process principle without turning it into a rigid project methodology.

core_concepts.name: Investigate the design before blaming the person
core_concepts.summary: Repeated human difficulty is evidence to inspect the system, task, feedback, constraints, and social setting.
core_concepts.distinct_diagnostic_value: Use when errors are being explained as carelessness, resistance, or lack of intelligence.
observable_user_behavior: Multiple users fail at the same point
People self-blame after ambiguous system behavior
Managers request more training before inspecting the workflow
core_concepts.specific_design_decision: Whether to redesign cues, constraints, state, and recovery before prescribing training.

source_traceability.source_file: The Design of Everyday Things Revised and Expanded Edition.epub(1).zip
source_traceability.book_title: The Design of Everyday Things: Revised and Expanded Edition
source_traceability.author: Don Norman
directly_supported_claims: The source argues that many so-called human errors should be investigated as design/system failures.

derivation.explanation: This record preserves the human-error framing while still requiring evidence for a particular diagnosis.

core_concepts.name: Training may compensate for missing system cues
core_concepts.summary: When repeated routine tasks need repeated explanations, the design may be moving knowledge into heads that belongs in the world.
core_concepts.distinct_diagnostic_value: Use when support, cheat sheets, or onboarding cover the same routine gap repeatedly.
observable_user_behavior: Users reopen the same instructions
Experts explain the same step every week
New users ask identical operational questions
core_concepts.specific_design_decision: Whether to externalize the explanation into labels, examples, constraints, defaults, or visible state.

source_traceability.chapter_title: Knowledge in the Head and in the World
source_traceability.section_heading: Knowledge in the Head and in the World
directly_supported_claims: Knowledge in the head can be efficient when learned, but it depends on memory and practice.
Knowledge in the world can reduce dependence on remembered information.
inferred_claims: Applies the source distinction to training dependence.

derivation.explanation: This is a source-grounded synthesis, not a direct claim about any current training program.

core_concepts.name: Design for error prevention and recovery
core_concepts.summary: Design should prevent predictable errors where possible and make recovery clear when errors occur.
core_concepts.distinct_diagnostic_value: Use when a system allows invalid states or makes repair expert-dependent.
observable_user_behavior: Users fear submitting
Wrong submissions require manual cleanup
After errors, users abandon or call an expert
core_concepts.specific_design_decision: Whether to add constraints, reversible actions, clearer error states, or targeted retry paths.

source_traceability.source_file: The Design of Everyday Things Revised and Expanded Edition.epub(1).zip
source_traceability.book_title: The Design of Everyday Things: Revised and Expanded Edition
source_traceability.author: Don Norman
directly_supported_claims: Constraints reduce the set of possible actions.
Design can reduce the chance and consequence of error.

derivation.explanation: This record joins prevention and recovery without making all mechanisms interchangeable.

core_concepts.name: Observed user behavior outranks abstract principle selection
core_concepts.summary: The reasoning OS should guide investigation, but current observations, tests, screenshots, logs, and user feedback determine diagnosis.
core_concepts.distinct_diagnostic_value: Use when an assistant is tempted to assert a diagnosis without behavioral evidence.
observable_user_behavior: Only a screenshot is available
A single anecdote is treated as proof
No user observation has occurred
core_concepts.specific_design_decision: Whether to recommend evidence collection before redesign.

core_concepts.name: Separate conceptual confidence from empirical diagnosis confidence
core_concepts.summary: A Norman concept may be strongly supported while a claim about a specific user behavior remains uncertain until observed.
core_concepts.distinct_diagnostic_value: Use when a design principle is clear but the available evidence is weak.
observable_user_behavior: A reviewer makes a plausible diagnosis from limited artifacts
An assistant states certainty from one behavior signal
core_concepts.specific_design_decision: Whether to label the recommendation as a hypothesis, direct principle, or verified diagnosis.
